subject: spanish
title: Stamp 2: Sincretismo Religioso
welcome_lead: Stamp the religious syncretism of Latin America.
meta_desc: A-Level Spanish adventure on religious syncretism and popular Catholicism in Latin America.

concepts.def: Religious syncretism: blending of Catholic, indigenous, and African beliefs.
Patroness of Mexico, appeared to Juan Diego in 1531; iconic syncretic figure.
Afro-Cuban religion blending Yoruba beliefs with Catholic saints.
Afro-Brazilian religion of Yoruba origin, recognised since the 19th century.
Mexican Day of the Dead (1-2 November); fuses indigenous and Catholic traditions.
Andean Mother Earth, venerated alongside Catholic figures in Bolivia and Peru.

walkthroughs.body_html: Spanish missionaries imposed Catholicism but indigenous and African believers retained pre-Christian practices. Saints overlapped with local deities. Sincretism emerged as a living adaptation, not mere imposition.

The Virgin's 1531 apparition at Tepeyac, on a hill previously sacred to the goddess Tonantzin, made her a powerful syncretic symbol. She became patroness of Mexico in 1737 and of Latin America in 1910.
On 1-2 November, families build altars (ofrendas) with marigolds, sugar skulls, and favourite foods of the deceased. UNESCO listed it as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2008.
